name: Destroy Lonely
label: Opium / Interscope
lede: The son of a Disturbing tha Peace rapper started recording at fourteen, got a call from [[Playboi Carti]] at nineteen, and has spent the years since turning Opium's black-on-black sound into what he calls sonic horror movies.

eras.title: Second-generation Atlanta
eras.text: Bobby Sandimanie III grows up around a rap career that came before his: his father recorded for Ludacris's Disturbing tha Peace. He spends his teens homeschooled, online and in a school studio, and puts out tape after tape before anyone outside Atlanta is listening.

years.src: Wikipedia: Destroy Lonely · Alternative Press · XXL: Inside Destroy Lonely's Dark, Cinematic World · Rolling Stone: Destroy Lonely Makes Whatever
years.h: Bobby Wardell Sandimanie III is born in Atlanta
years.p: His father is I-20, a rapper signed to Ludacris's Disturbing tha Peace in the late 1990s, who turns up on Ludacris's 2002 single "Move Bitch."
years.xp:
Wikipedia gives Atlanta as his birthplace and notes Liberian descent, two younger half-sisters and an older half-brother. Alternative Press has him born in Decatur, Georgia, and later moving to Atlanta's southside to live with his grandmother.

Rolling Stone gives the father's name as Infamous 2-0; XXL and Wikipedia call him I-20.

years.src: XXL: Destroy Lonely Interview · Wikipedia: Destroy Lonely
years.h: A production class turns into a rap career
years.p: At fourteen he starts making music in his school's studio, where he meets producers Texaco and Nezzus. Production didn't click, so he started rapping instead.
years.xp:
XXL says he cared more about video games and fashion than music at first, and that his first raps went down on a broken laptop in his bedroom with a classmate producing. He was homeschooled from sixth grade, with public school for ninth and tenth.

Per Wikipedia, "Destroy" comes from feeling that drug use was destroying him, and "Lonely" from the years he spent alone as a kid.

years.src: Wikipedia: Destroy Lonely · XXL: Destroy Lonely Interview
years.h: Darkhorse, the first tape, lands in the same year as "Bane"
years.p: The mixtape opens a run of releases that barely pauses for two years. "Bane," also from 2019, is the song that catches on first.
years.xp: XXL calls "Bane" his breakout single and says it went viral on TikTok in early 2021, two years after it came out.

eras.title: Carti picks up the phone
eras.text: Five mixtapes and a pile of EPs in one year, then a video that reaches the right person. By early 2021 he is one of the first names on Playboi Carti's new label.

years.p: One of five mixtapes he puts out in 2020, after Underworld in March. A sequel follows on Halloween, and the series is still running in 2025.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Destroy Lonely Makes Whatever · XXL: Destroy Lonely Interview · XXL: Inside Destroy Lonely's Dark, Cinematic World
years.h: The "Oh Yeah" video reaches Playboi Carti
years.p: Carti sees it and wants a meeting. Destroy Lonely tells Rolling Stone that when they met, Carti said he wanted to sign him, and the two recorded about 20 songs.
years.xp: To XXL he describes Carti as someone who told him to keep his head straight because Carti had been there before. In 2026 he calls Carti "genuinely my big brother."

years.src: Rolling Stone: Destroy Lonely Makes Whatever · Wikipedia: Destroy Lonely
years.h: He signs to Opium, Carti's label inside Interscope
years.p: He joins [[Ken Carson|860d7dc2-618d-437e-a3bb-7b91c2d40095]] among the first artists on Opium. That April he appears in Carti's "Sky" video.

eras.title: A stylist he doesn't need, a horror movie he does
eras.text: A surprise mixtape and a TikTok hit make him Opium's next name, and a month in New York produces 120 songs and a debut album built like a slasher film.

years.cap: Destroy Lonely on the No Stylist Tour, Patio Theater, Chicago, December 2022
years.h: On the road with Ken Carson for the X Man Tour
years.p: He's on Carson's X that July, then the No Stylist Tour gets announced in October.

q: I'm just making whatever the hell I want.
years.src: Wikipedia: No Stylist · Rolling Stone: Destroy Lonely Makes Whatever
years.h: No Stylist drops with no warning and goes Gold
years.p: Nineteen tracks, one guest ([[Ken Carson|860d7dc2-618d-437e-a3bb-7b91c2d40095]]), a No. 91 debut on the Billboard 200. The title song goes viral on TikTok.
years.xp: Rolling Stone puts his monthly Spotify listeners past 2.6 million on the strength of "NOSTYLIST." A deluxe, NS+ (Ultra), adds five songs that November. Critics were mixed: AllMusic gave it 1.5 out of 5.

q: This ain't nothing but sonic horror movies.
years.src: Wikipedia: If Looks Could Kill · Alternative Press
years.h: If Looks Could Kill debuts at No. 18
years.p: The debut album runs 78 minutes under an alter ego, Look Killa, and comes with a short film of the same name. First-week count: 29,398 units.
years.xp:
It came out of about six weeks in New York in October and November 2022, where he recorded more than 120 songs with his producers, his girlfriend and his best friends in the room. [[Clayco|decfaeba-f5c2-4f4d-8ac3-afa13a1ca795]] and TM88 are among the producers.

He told Alternative Press it's horror movies in sound form. Pitchfork gave it 5.7 and called it overlong; Alternative Press said he was finally hitting his stride. A Director's Cut added six songs on September 29.

eras.title: Top ten, then the Opium arena run
eras.text: His second album goes top ten and the reviews stay rough. In 2025 he goes back to mixtapes and finally lands a credited song with Carti, then opens arenas for him.

years.h: Love Lasts Forever is his first top-ten album
years.p: No. 10 on the Billboard 200 and No. 1 on the R&B/Hip-Hop albums chart, on 37,500 first-week units. Lil 88 produces every track.
years.xp: [[Lil Uzi Vert|8837b875-3689-4646-b3fd-d8b53815c7a8]] guests on "Love Hurts" and [[Ken Carson|860d7dc2-618d-437e-a3bb-7b91c2d40095]] also appears; [[Don Toliver|a0723a3c-4135-438e-85c5-012712144ede]] is on the CD edition. Pitchfork gave it 4.5.

years.h: A gas-station argument with Shannade Clermont goes viral
years.p: The clip shows him trying to get into a car she has locked. Clermont posts that he did not hit her and that he was mad she locked him out.
years.xp: HotNewHipHop notes he had faced domestic abuse allegations from an ex-girlfriend earlier in 2024; Wikipedia says he denied them.

years.h: "Off the Meter" is his first credited song with Carti
years.p: It's on [[Ken Carson|860d7dc2-618d-437e-a3bb-7b91c2d40095]]'s More Chaos, with all three Opium names credited. It peaks at No. 11 on Bubbling Under.
A third broken-heart tape, with one guest ([[Ken Carson|860d7dc2-618d-437e-a3bb-7b91c2d40095]] on "Open It Up") and 33 producers. It reaches No. 64.
years.xp: He'd told Clash it was a mixtape for the existing fans, more personal and less polished than the albums. "Jumanji" came a week earlier with a video.

years.cap: Destroy Lonely at the Fillmore, Philadelphia, January 2025
years.src: Wikipedia: Antagonist Tour · XXL: Inside Destroy Lonely's Dark, Cinematic World
years.p: Thirty-one North American shows through December 1, with [[Ken Carson|860d7dc2-618d-437e-a3bb-7b91c2d40095]], Homixide Gang and Apollo Red1 also on the bill.
years.xp: The tour had been announced in 2023 and canceled in March 2024 before coming back in 2025 as a domestic arena run. Chicago, New York and Newark sold out; in Los Angeles, [[Kendrick Lamar|381086ea-f511-4aba-bdf9-71c753dc5077]] joined Carti onstage.

eras.title: Working on Drop Dead Gorgeous
eras.text: The third album is being built in a Midtown Manhattan studio, and he's calling it his hardest work yet.

years.cap: Destroy Lonely at his afterparty in Orlando, May 2026
years.src: XXL: Inside Destroy Lonely's Dark, Cinematic World
years.h: Drop Dead Gorgeous takes shape in Midtown Manhattan
years.p: He tells XXL it's the most difficult music he's made, with [[Clayco|decfaeba-f5c2-4f4d-8ac3-afa13a1ca795]] on most beats and Cxdy and Snow Strippers on others.
years.xp: He names My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy, Lauryn Hill, 1990s rap, DJ Screw and EDM as touchstones and calls it the most Destroy Lonely album he has made. XXL said it was likely to come out in 2026.
